UnderstandingPrompt: Village goods output means all actual goods generated by the native production model in administratively attached villages, including village-type products, horses and other livestock, and common grain, cheese and butter batches. Select only if the policy directly changes agriculture, animal husbandry, breeding, gathering, raw-material processing or food-goods output. Do not mistake town food stocks, workshop production speed, construction power or mere trade circulation for village output. Only the production model changes; goods first enter village inventories and circulate through native villager transport and TradeBound markets.
EvaluationPrompt: The value is a percentage change relative to the final current native village goods output, not a fixed item count. Native base daily village output is low and actual inventory additions use randomized rounding, so positive policies need perceptible intensity. Do not assess clearly effective policies at only +5% to +15%. +20 multiplies output by 1.2, +50 by 1.5, +100 by 2, and -100 sets it to zero. Mild tools, road maintenance or seasonal support usually use +20% to +40%, or -10% to -20% for negatives. Explicit agricultural, husbandry or breeding institutions use about +40% to +80%, or -20% to -40%. Large irrigation, land reform or strong production reforms use about +80% to +150%; forced requisition, severe labor loss or disasters use -40% to -70%. Extreme positive policies changing regional economic structure may reach +150% to +250%; devastating disasters or total plunder use -70% to -100%. Add policies first; the multiplier minimum is 0 and there is no extra positive hard cap, but negative assessments must not be below -100%.
